title: Production assurance voice lab: homepage & product messaging experiments
body:
Objective:
Run a set of lightweight copy experiments aimed at proving the value proposition most persuasive to engineering and platform buyers: predictable latency + unit economics + operational controls. We want a compact hero and a clear product-level lead into the UI/console and pricing pages.

Primary hypothesis:
Messaging that foregrounds measurable operational outcomes (latency SLOs, per-token cost ranges, fallbacks) will convert better for developer and platform audiences than feature-led copy alone.

Audience slices (prioritized):
- Developer/engineer (early integrator): values fast onboarding, SDK ergonomics, low-friction trials.
- Platform/infra owner (decision influencer): cares about predictability, SLAs, private deployment controls.
- Product managers (buyer champion): cares about time-to-market and reliability of critical features.

Hero concept A — "Predictable inference. Measurable outcomes."
Headlines (short):
- "Predictable inference, engineered for production."
- "Latency you can bank on. Costs you can measure."
Subheads (longer):
- "Ship LLM features with SLO-driven serving, automated fallbacks, and per-route cost insights—so product teams stop guessing and start delivering."
- "A single API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with cost & latency controls built into the runtime."
Voice notes: authoritative, empirical, low-ceremony.
Best placement: top of homepage; test with a small animated metric strip (latency SLOs, unit cost delta).

Hero concept B — "Treat inference like core infra."
Headlines (short):
- "Run inference like you run databases."
- "Enterprise-grade inference controls for developer teams."
Subheads:
- "Reserved capacity, autoscaling policies, rolling rollouts, and predictable unit economics—so inference is a platform capability, not a risk."
- "Private deployment options and KMS integrations for regulated workloads."
Voice notes: pragmatic, slightly formal, resonates with SRE/infra leads.

Hero concept C — "Ship faster. Spend less. Stay online."
Headlines:
- "Speed, cost, and reliability—balanced by design."
- "Deliver LLM features without the ops overhead."
Subheads:
- "Intelligent batching, KV caching, and model routing reduce token spend while keeping latency tight."
- "Automatic fallbacks and canary rollouts keep customer experiences consistent during incidents."
Voice notes: outcome-oriented, product-obsessed.

Product page: "Redwood Dedicated" lead paragraph variants:
- "Dedicated capacity that behaves like a predictable cluster: reserved GPUs, configurable autoscaling policies, and SLAs for latency and throughput. Ideal when consistency matters more than raw bench numbers."
- "Reserved pools, deterministic latency, and enterprise-safe networking—designed to make inference an internal platform service."

Core proof points (short bullets) to surface near hero/footer:
- "Latency SLOs: configurable percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per-route"
- "Per-token unit economics: live cost breakdown by model + batching"
- "Fallbacks and model variants: automated routing to compatible variants when capacity constrained"
- "Private deployment options: VPC-ready control plane + on-prem package"
- "Integrations: KMS/HSM, Datadog, Prometheus, GitHub Actions"

Competitive differentiation matrix (copy-friendly bullets):
- Compared to managed LLM APIs: focus on production economics (batching, KV cache, cost attribution) rather than model novelty.
- Compared to self-hosted runtimes: provide first-class observability, rollout tooling, and SLA-backed dedicated capacity.
- Compared to cloud ML endpoints: simpler developer ergonomics and predictable per-token economics.

Suggested test matrix (priority experiments):
1) Hero headline A vs B vs C (A/B/C) — metric: signups from developer landing, secondary: time-to-first-API-call.
2) Proof strip vs no-proof strip (adds micro-metrics under hero: p95 latency, typical cost per 1k tokens) — metric: CTA click-through.
3) Short technical subhead vs benefits-led subhead for product page (Dedicated) — metric: Demo requests & Enterprise interest form fills.
4) CTA wording: "Get started free" vs "Request dedicated capacity" vs "Estimate cost" — metric: funnel movement by cohort.

Measurement plan:
- Primary signal: developer signups and first API call within 24h.
- Secondary signals: demo requests, enterprise contact forms, time in docs (engagement), and QA-driven eval submissions.
- Stat threshold: 95% confidence with min detectable effect of 7% uplift on primary signal.

Canonical microcopy recommendations (compact):
- Button: "Start free" (dev), "Request capacity" (platform), "Talk to sales" (enterprise)
- Micro-CTA under hero: "See typical latency & cost for your workload" (links to small interactive calculator)
- Trustline: "SLA-backed dedicated capacity • VPC/private deployments • Bring-your-own-key"

Page scaffolding suggestions (order):
1) Hero (headline + 1-liner + primary CTA + proof strip)
2) 3-line product summary (hosted / dedicated / private) with quick-compare tiles
3) Short technical highlights (batching, caching, routing) with one-sentence impact lines
4) Customer stories / use cases (short blurbs)
5) Pricing snapshot & cost calculator teaser
6) Docs + SDK quickstart CTA

Example short customer blurb (for use on homepage):
- "How Frey Health reduced inference spend 42% while improving p95 latency by 35% using Redwood's KV cache and autoscaling policies."

Risk & guardrails:
- Avoid overclaiming benchmarks without context—always pair numbers with workload footprint (sequence length, model family, batch strategy).
- Don’t promise absolute cost numbers; present ranges and median-case examples.
- Keep hero copy lean; detailed operational claims belong on product/tech pages.

Next actions for the sprint:
- Finalize three hero variants and produce lightweight A/B tests (Mar 9) — design to handoff by Mar 11.
- Implement proof-strip component in staging and populate with synthetic but realistic metrics (Mar 16).
- Wire up event tracking and funnel metrics (Mar 18).
- Draft Dedicated page technical bullets and hand to docs for deeper explainer (Mar 22).

Notes / open questions:
- Do we have an up-to-date median p95 latency benchmark for our curated models to populate the proof strip? (ask infra team: SRE-serve)
- Should the calculator surface committed-capacity savings vs on-demand hosted? (product input required)

Reference copy snippets (to borrow/adapt):
- "Predictable SLAs for inference—so product teams can own feature SLAs like any other backend service."
- "Cost transparency by route and token—measure and optimize the true economics of your features."

Appendix: sample micro-test content for experimentation (copy-ready)
- Variant A hero headline: "Predictable inference, engineered for production."
- Variant A subhead: "SLOs, fallbacks, and cost visibility—one API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- CTA: "Start free"

- Variant B hero headline: "Run inference like infrastructure."
- Variant B subhead: "Dedicated capacity and private deployments with enterprise controls and SLAs."
- CTA: "Request capacity"

- Variant C hero headline: "Balance speed, cost, and reliability."
- Variant C subhead: "Intelligent batching, KV caching, and model routing to reduce unit spend and preserve latency."
- CTA: "Estimate cost"

Contact: Aisha Patel (lead), + collaborators for final review.
